speakers.voiceDescription: A man in his mid-thirties, American, from somewhere flat and Midwestern. Tired and a little hoarse after six hours behind the wheel at night, soft-spoken and close to the microphone, as if talking to himself inside a small car. An ordinary, decent man, not a hero: when he is frightened the voice thins, catches and drops to a whisper, his breathing goes shallow, but he keeps it low and holds himself together. Dry, intimate, no reverb.
speakers.previewText: Come on... come on, don't do this to me. Forty-eight miles to anything, and the needle's been sitting under the E since the county line. There's a light up there on the rise. A sign. Rooms. Okay. Okay, that's fine, somebody's awake at least. They'll have to put me up for the night. I'll pay whatever they want, I just need somewhere dry until morning.

speakers.voiceDescription: An old rural American man in his sixties, big-chested and stooped. A deep, gravelly, nearly toneless monotone; slow words with long gaps between them and heavy breath through the nose. Quiet, patient menace, never raises his voice, sounds worn down to the bone. Flat Plains accent. Muffled and close, as though he is speaking through a coarse burlap sack pulled over his head.
speakers.previewText: Rain's been on the road since noon. They always come in the rain. You hear the bell, you come on in, that's all there is to it. I don't do the taking. Never did. I just keep the door and I keep the book, and I sharpen what needs sharpening. Go on, then. Go on up. She'll find you, friend. She always does.

speakers.voiceDescription: A woman in her late twenties from a small rural town in 1970s America, a seamstress. Warm, low and slightly husky; exhausted but quietly determined, choosing each word with care, with a thread of dry humour under the tiredness. Intimate and unhurried, close to the microphone. When she whispers the voice becomes breathy, wet and broken, catching on the edges of the words.
speakers.previewText: Ruthie, it's late and my hands are shaking, so forgive the writing. I've got it all worked out this time. Tuesday, the six-ten, the early one, before he's up. I've sewn what matters where he won't look. Don't write back to the house. Don't tell Mama. Just be there, at the depot, the way you promised, and if I'm late, wait for me. I'll come. Whatever it takes, I'll come.

speakers.voiceDescription: A woman in her forties, American, polite and nervous, rain-soaked and short of breath from hurrying up a porch in a storm. Mid-pitched, slightly apologetic, trying hard to sound friendly to a stranger's door late at night. Natural and clear, close to the microphone.
speakers.previewText: Oh, thank God. Rooms. Okay. Hello? Hi, I'm so sorry, I know how late it is, I saw the sign from the road. My car ran out of gas about a mile back, and there's nothing out here, no phone, nothing. I can pay. I just need somewhere dry until it's light. Hello? Is anyone there? I heard the bell ring. I'm sorry to bother you.

lines.text: [tired, under his breath] Come on... [exhales] come on, don't do this to me.
lines.subtitle: Come on… come on, don't do this to me.

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [quietly, to himself] Forty-eight miles to anything... [sighs] They'll have to put me up for the night.

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [flat, tired, to the radio] Nothing. Not even a preacher.
lines.subtitle: Nothing. Not even a preacher.

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [under his breath, finger on the map] Should've stayed on the interstate.
lines.subtitle: Should've stayed on the interstate.

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [squinting, sharp] Dim your lights—
lines.subtitle: Dim your lights—

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [raising his voice over the rain, hesitant] Hello? [short pause] ...Sorry to bother you this late. My car ran out of gas.
lines.subtitle: Hello? …Sorry to bother you this late. My car ran out of gas.

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [panicked, breathless whisper] No, no, no, come on, open—
lines.subtitle: No, no, no, come on, open—

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [whispers, shaking] Don't breathe. [short, shaky breath] Don't breathe.
lines.subtitle: Don't breathe. Don't breathe.

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [barely audible, stunned] That's... [swallows] that's my car.
lines.subtitle: That's… that's my car.

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [reading under his breath] Carvel, six-ten... Tuesday, October twelfth. [pause] Nineteen seventy-six.
lines.subtitle: Carvel, 6:10… Tuesday, October 12th. 1976.

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [whispers] R-V-X... [swallows hard] that's my plate.
lines.subtitle: RVX… that's my plate.

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [a shaking, pleading whisper] Look. [breath] It's him. [breath] It's him you want.
lines.subtitle: Look. It's him. It's him you want.

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [half laughing, half crying] Come on... come on— [exhales hard] yes. Yes.
lines.subtitle: Come on… come on— yes. Yes.
lines.previousText: Come on... come on, don't do this to me.

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [slow, tired breathing through the nose] Hhh... hhh...
lines.caption: (breathing)

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [fast, shallow, frightened breathing] Hh— hh— hhh— hh—
lines.caption: (frightened breathing)

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [sharp inhale, then holds his breath] Hhp— mm.
lines.caption: (holds breath)

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [straining to hold his breath, a tiny leak through the nose] Mmm— mm—
lines.caption: (straining to hold breath)

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [slow, silent, shaking exhale, trying not to make a sound] Hhhhh...
lines.caption: (shaky exhale)

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [a sudden gasp for air he can't hold back] Hhah—!
lines.caption: (gasps)

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [panting hard after running, trying to be quiet] Hah... hah... hah... hah...
lines.caption: (panting)

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [a stifled whimper, lips pressed shut] Mm— nnh.
lines.caption: (stifled whimper)

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [startled sharp intake of breath, frozen] Hh—
lines.caption: (sharp breath)

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [a sharp intake of breath that stops dead, then nothing, he cannot breathe]  Hh—
lines.caption: (breath catches)

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [quiet grunt of effort through clenched teeth] Nngh... hhn...
lines.caption: (straining)

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [choking, a wet hand over his mouth, drowning] Hgh— ghh— mmf—
lines.caption: (choking)

lines.speaker: driver
lines.text: [a long, trembling exhale of disbelief] Hhhhhh... oh...
lines.caption: (trembling breath)

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: [a wet, broken whisper, searching] ...Harlan?
lines.subtitle: …Harlan?

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: [whispers, inches away, trembling, waterlogged] Har... lan?
lines.subtitle: …Harlan?

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: [a disappointed, gurgling exhale, water in the throat] Hhhh— ghh...
lines.caption: (a wet, disappointed breath)

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: [slow, bubbling, waterlogged breathing] Hhhh... hhhh...
lines.caption: (wet breathing)

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: [a low gurgle deep in the throat] Ghhhh...
lines.caption: (gurgling, close)

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: [ragged, wet, gasping breaths while lurching forward] Hah— hhah— hah—
lines.caption: (ragged wet breathing, coming fast)

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: [barely a whisper, forehead against the wood] ...my room...
lines.subtitle: …my room…

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: [whispering, wet, drifting] ...where are you...
lines.subtitle: …where are you…

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: [whispering against a door, patient, wet] ...Harlan... I hear you...
lines.subtitle: …Harlan… I hear you…

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: [a sudden wet rush of breath right against the face] Hhhaaah—
lines.caption: (a wet breath against your face)

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: [a near-sob, wet and breaking, almost no voice] ...my ticket... [a shuddering, bubbling breath] hhh...
lines.subtitle: …my ticket…

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: [a long wet breath, then softly, with terrible certainty] ...Harlan.
lines.subtitle: …Harlan.

lines.speaker: ada
lines.text: [warm, tired, determined, reading her own letter aloud] Ruthie. Tuesday, the six-ten to Carvel. He found the tin, so the ticket's sewn in the hem of my wedding dress, with the locket. [pause] I can't wear his face anymore, but I won't leave it for him. [quieter] He says he'll put me down the well first. [a small, defiant breath] Let him try. I'll be at the depot if I have to wa—

lines.speaker: harlan
lines.text: [low, slow, flat, through a burlap sack] Go on, then.
lines.subtitle: Go on, then.

lines.speaker: harlan
lines.text: [slow, muffled, tilting his head up toward the ceiling] She'll find you, friend. [a long breath through the sack] She always does.
lines.subtitle: She'll find you, friend. She always does.

lines.speaker: harlan
lines.text: [flat, patient, calling through the wall over a ringing bell] Come on, Ada. [pause] Company.
lines.subtitle: Come on, Ada. Company.

lines.speaker: harlan
lines.text: [a startled, hoarse whisper through the sack] Ada?... [his breath catches] No. No, no—
lines.subtitle: Ada?… No. No, no—

lines.speaker: harlan
lines.text: [slow, flat, reading his own ledger, tired] October fourteen, seventy-six. She came up out of the well. [pause] Did like Mother's book says: took the head, gave it back to the water. Holds her one night. [pause] Nailed her room shut. She can't get past nails, just stands there scratching. [low] I won't go in either.

lines.speaker: harlan
lines.text: [slow, flat, reading] She can't find me if she can't see me. Covered the glass. Cut myself out of the pictures. Sleep in the sack. [pause] She goes close to every face she finds, hunting mine. [lower, almost afraid] If she ever sees it she'll know me, and that's the end of me. [pause] Only picture left went down the well with her. In her locket.

lines.speaker: harlan
lines.text: [slow, flat, reading] Every pull in the house rings in the parlor now. She always comes to the bell. [pause] Always did. [pause] She can't hear a thing under thunder. [pause] The drifter kept her quiet a month. Did the Pruitt boy myself; didn't hold her an hour. She has to take them herself. [a long breath] She works the latches now. [quietly] She learns.
